description: An adaptation of Sandoval's conjecture mapping tool, created by Chang and Roschelle, that supports interdisciplinary design-based research teams in connecting learning theory to technical design.
title: Adapted conjecture map framework for learning scientists and computer scientists

description: A taxonomy for structuring research agendas in education, adapted from Miles's (2017) seven-dimension research gap framework by collapsing the Knowledge and Theoretical gaps and the Empirical and Evidence gaps into single dimensions.
title: Adapted five-dimension research gap analysis framework for education

description: A risk-of-bias assessment instrument adapted from a tool developed by Hombrados & Waddington (2012), used to code and critically appraise the quality of quantitative effectiveness studies before meta-analysis.
title: Adapted Hombrados & Waddington risk-of-bias assessment tool

description: The study adapts Shen et al.'s (2015) interdisciplinary reasoning and communication (IRC) framework for novice high-school students rather than experts.
title: Adapted IRC framework for novice students' interdisciplinary reasoning

description: The article adapts the Personalized Learning Continuum Framework of Lokey-Vega and Stephens (2019) as an analytical lens for classifying AI-enabled personalized learning models along the proportion of Academic Learning Time spent on automated versus student-centered pedagogies and the distribution o
title: Adapted Personalized Learning Continuum Framework (PLCF)
Adapted S.P.A.R.K. model for coding peer feedback quality

description: The article adapts a process evaluation framework proposed by Steckler and Linnan to structure its mixed-methods evaluation of the training.
title: Adapted Steckler and Linnan process evaluation framework

description: The article adapts Talbot et al.'s seven-class virtual patient taxonomy into a one-dimensional classification with two levels of description.
title: Adapted virtual patient classification framework with seven classes described on two levels: predominant competency and predominant technology

description: Adaptive G-UKT is a knowledge tracing framework that models each learner's evolving latent state as a Gaussian distribution rather than a point vector, tracking \"semantic activation levels and estimation confidence through diagonal covariance\".
title: Adaptive G-UKT

description: The article argues that non-adaptive control variants fail to control for expectancy, motivation and demand effects because adaptive trainees are constantly challenged and see their improvement.
title: Adaptive unrelated-capacity control-group design for cognitive training trials

description: Where jurisdictions lack longitudinal achievement data because surveys are costly, intrusive, and suffer attrition, the article recommends creating representative data by linking large-scale administrative databases under clear protocols and validation procedures.
title: Administrative data linkage for longitudinal educational research
